stories.headline: PT approves 2026 election manifesto at 8th National Congress, focusing on Lula reelection
stories.summary: The Workers' Party held its 8th National Congress in Brasília (April 24-26), approving a manifesto focused on Lula's reelection and laying out strategic priorities. Party leadership worked to minimize internal conflict by excluding controversial topics, with Lula participating via video due to medical procedures.

stories.headline: President Lula undergoes skin cancer removal and wrist treatment at São Paulo hospital
stories.summary: President Lula underwent surgical procedures on April 24 at Hospital Sírio-Libanês in São Paulo, removing a basocelular carcinoma (most common type of skin cancer) from his scalp and receiving infiltration treatment for wrist tendonitis. He was discharged without complications and returned to Brasília on April 26.

stories.headline: Brazil-US diplomatic crisis escalates over Alexandre Ramagem's detention in Florida
stories.summary: Former ABIN director Alexandre Ramagem was arrested in Florida on April 13 but released after two days, prompting a diplomatic incident. The US subsequently expelled Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, who was involved in Ramagem's capture. Brazil applied reciprocity by withdrawing credentials from US agent Michael Myers, escalating tensions in bilateral law enforcement cooperation.

stories.headline: 2026 presidential race: Flávio Bolsonaro gains in key states while Lula's approval declines in some regions
stories.summary: Recent polling data shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) advancing against incumbent President Lula in multiple scenarios. In Rio de Janeiro, Flávio leads in both first and second-round polls. In São Paulo, the gap has narrowed. Lula's approval ratings show regional variation, with weaker performance in the Northeast and in youth demographics.

stories.headline: Finance Ministry blocks prediction markets and regulates critical minerals without tax breaks
stories.summary: Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced two major regulatory actions: blocking access to international prediction market platforms Polymarket and Kalshi to prevent 'bet-like' speculation, and establishing regulations for critical minerals extraction that do not include new tax incentives, aiming instead to secure national sovereignty.

stories.headline: Fernando Haddad discusses vice-presidential candidates for São Paulo race

Internal polling showed Tebet performing well with target voters. Haddad attacked Flávio Bolsonaro as 'Bolsonarinho' during PT Congress.

stories.summary: Petrobras signed a new shareholders' agreement with Shine I fund regarding control of Braskem petrochemical company. The state oil company chose not to exercise its preference and tag-along rights when former shareholder Novonor sold its controlling stake, allowing IG4 Capital's fund to gain control.

stories.headline: Bank Master failure triggers pension fund restrictions and organized crime investigation
stories.summary: Following the collapse of Banco Master, one of Brazil's largest bank failures in recent history, financial regulators imposed stringent restrictions on public pension funds that were creditors. The bank's liquidation triggered investigations into alleged links between the institution and organized crime, expanding the scandal's implications.

stories.headline: Government rejects PT proposal for new Terrabras state enterprise for critical minerals
stories.summary: The Lula administration decided not to support the creation of Terrabras, a new state enterprise for controlling and refining critical minerals, breaking with a proposal favored by sections of the PT. Finance Ministry and economic authorities argued that Brazil's strong global demand for rare earths does not require additional state infrastructure.

stories.headline: PT sues TSE to remove 'Dona Maria' AI persona attacking Lula on social media
stories.summary: The PT coalition (PT, PV, PCdoB) filed a complaint with the Electoral Superior Court (TSE) requesting removal of social media profiles using an AI-generated elderly Black woman persona ('Dona Maria') to attack President Lula and leftist figures. The federation claims the profiles represent illegal advance electoral propaganda and disinformation campaigns.
